title: 8.	RISK REDUCING SURGERY FOR WOMEN @ RISK OF EPITHELIAL TUMOR

blocks.content:
8.RISK REDUCING SURGERY FOR WOMEN @ RISK OF EPITHELIAL TUMOR
1.Protective factors:
•COC:
-20% after 5 years of use.
-50% after 15 years of use
-Effect last for 30 years after cessation.
•Hysterectomy 34% in risk
•Tubal ligation 34% in risk
•Ligation + COC = 72% ed in risk
•BRCA + tubal ligation = 60%
•B.F over 12m0 risk.
1.Risk Factors:
•Fx strongest factor – present in 10 – 15%.
-1 member affected = 4 – 5%.
-2 members affected = 7%.
-General population =1.7%

Breast CA Herediary syndromes

•BRCA 1=35 – 46% 90% Of heredity.
•BRCA 2=13 – 23% cancers
•Lynch Syndrome 3 – 14%.
•HNPCC = 1%
•Puetz – Jagher – 20%

OTHER RISK FACTORS

•Ovulation induction – BOT.
•Endometriosis.
•Obesity.
•PCOD.

Screening NR Routinely:

•Predictive value 3%.
•Undertaken in women who decline Risk Reducing surgery.
⇨TVS + CA -125 every 6m0 from 35 years of age.
⇨Or 5 – 10 years earlier than earliest age of 1st diagnosis of ovarian CA in family.

10% risk of CA ovary go for => rrBSO.

30% risk of CA Breast go for => risk reducing Mastectomy.

Risk of ovarian CA:

1. Increased Risk

•positive Fx
-single member 4 – 5%.
-2 members 7%.
•General population 1.7%.

2.High risk

•Hereditary cancers in Family
•Referral to Geneticists + screening of BRCA or HNPCC.
•Ovarian Risk = 13 – 50%.
•BRCA 1 = 35 – 46%.
•BRCA 2 = 13 – 23%.

HNPCC & lynch 3 – 14%.

Suggested Management:

1.Increased Risk group:

•No screening
•Consider risk reducing BSO (rrBSO) on individualized consideration involving Pt & Clinician.

2.High Risk group:

•No screening except those who decline rrBSO.

BRCA – 1:

1.Offer rrBSO @ 35 years when child bearing is completed
2.Protective effect on CA Breast (risk reduction is 30 – 75% in CA Breast).

BRCA – 2:

•rrBSO after 35 years can be delayed up till 45 years but delay would lose the benefit of risk reduction in CA Breast.

HNPCC & Lynch:

-Bowel = 40 – 60%.
-Ovary = 10 – 20%.
-Uterus = 40 – 60%.
•rrBSO + TAH due to risk of Endometrial CA 40 – 60%.

 

•Chemoprevention Aspirin from 16 years of age.
•Colonoscopy every 2 years after 25 – 30 years.
•H – pylori testing after HNPCC positive
•Role of PGD.
•Role of PND.

Risk Reducing Surgery:

•rrBSO recommended:
-30 – 75% reduction in CA Breast.
-2% risk of primary peritoneal cancer.
•Salpingectomy – if ovaries need to be preserved.
•Radical Fimbriectomy – if Pt refuses BSO.
-Removal of fimbria at ovarian junction.
•Concurrent TAH is recommended when:
-Lynch syndrome
-Prophylactically, if chemo is required for CA Breast (tamoxifen)
-When ERT is given for hormone replacement purpose,(progesterone increase risk of CA Breast).
•Mastectomy
-Progesterone is avoided in HRT as it es risk of CA breast.

Chemoprevention:

•Pt with hereditary ovarian cancer syndrome who have not elected for rrBSO or are trying to conceive.

 

Pre – Op Evaluation before rrBSO:

•Occult Malignancy 4 – 8%.
•Rule out occult malignancy by TVS and CA – 125.

Surgical Procedure:

•BSO by removing all ovarian and tubal tissue except intramyometrial part.
•ligate ovarian Artery 2cm away from ovary @ pelvic brim.

Menopause and HRT:

⇨Recommended.
•HRT up to 51 years.
•Small in CA Breast but low overall and no impact on mortality.

Factors to reduce CA Breast on HRT:

•Concurrent TAH.
•Mastectomy.
•Limiting use of HRT.
⇨BRCA – 1 Carrier has CA Breast that is typically E and P receptor negative.
⇨BRCA – 2 carriers are usually positive.

Recovery:

•After BSO – 3M0.
•Mastectomy – 3m0.
